species.real: Bernard Lovell moved his radar kit out to Jodrell Bank because the electric trams in Manchester made too much interference for him to hear anything from space.
species.name: Bleeplet

dex.text: Sits in a field on clear nights with its dish turned up, listening very hard to absolutely nothing. Says it heard a star. Nobody can prove it didn't.
dex.fact: Jodrell Bank in Cheshire began in 1945 with leftover army radar sets, and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

species.real: In 1966 Jodrell Bank picked up the first pictures from the Moon's surface, sent by the Soviet probe Luna 9, and they appeared in a British newspaper before the Soviets had released them.
species.name: Skyharker

dex.text: A great white dish on a lattice of iron, turning slowly over the Cheshire plain. When it swings round to look at you, you feel very small and slightly overheard.
dex.fact: The Lovell Telescope at Jodrell Bank has a dish 76 metres across. Finished in 1957, that October it tracked the rocket that carried Sputnik 1 into orbit.
